doc.title: Dorothy Donegan — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The Village Vanguard and Japanese audiences in the 1990s
summary: She treats Lorraine Gordon's Vanguard booking as just another gig, and notes Japanese fans arriving in droves.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: How about in the early 1990’s? It seems the cycle comes around every few years. New popularity. George Weins’ Kool Jazz Festival, at Carnegie Hall, Lorraine Gordon booking you into the Village Vanguard. Tell me about that.
What did I do at the Vanguard?
Is it a big deal that you’re playing at the Vanguard or is it just another gig?
It’s just another gig. They all are gigs.
These are a little more high profile. Do these high profile gigs help bring you new audiences?
Now I’m getting a Japanese audience.
They bring them there in droves. And they watch me and they seem to like it.
